subject.title: Add a slim Docker image mode with configurable APT package installation

question: Should OpenClaw support deployer-configured APT packages for pulled official Docker images, and should that be a derived-image prebuild flow rather than a startup-time installer?
rationale: The choice affects official image hardening, root package-manager execution, downtime, and the documented env/CLI contract, so source inspection cannot safely pick the product/security boundary.

options.title: Design a derived-image prebuild flow
options.body: Keep the issue open and specify a command or documented Dockerfile extension pattern that builds from the official image before restarting the gateway.

options.title: Allow startup-time installation
options.body: Add an explicit first-boot or entrypoint installer with caching, logging, failure semantics, and clear downtime/security warnings.

options.title: Keep build-time customization only
options.body: Defer or close this direction and continue steering operators to local builds or custom Dockerfiles for extra system packages.

recommendation.title: Design a derived-image prebuild flow
recommendation.body: Keep the issue open and specify a command or documented Dockerfile extension pattern that builds from the official image before restarting the gateway.

likelyOwner.reason: He merged and polished the existing optional APT package build-time contract, making him the best available routing candidate from the observed history.
